actual_parent_EC_guidance.when: FEDERAL is an allowable namespace and the asset is property of the debtor.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.procedure: Evaluate every applicable specific paragraph, then independently include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), which can protect any property. A dollar ceiling limits protection rather than eligibility. Thus a vehicle remains eligible under § 522(d)(2) above its cap, jewelry uses § 522(d)(4), and § 522(d)(5) remains an additional alternative even when a specific paragraph applies.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not use 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3) for an unlisted category such as a firearm or jewelry, do not omit a specific paragraph because value exceeds its ceiling, and do not repeat a citation.

actual_proposed_EC_guidance.when: FEDERAL is an allowable namespace and the asset is property of the debtor.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.procedure: Evaluate every applicable specific paragraph, then independently include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), which can protect any property. A dollar ceiling limits protection rather than eligibility. Thus a vehicle remains eligible under § 522(d)(2) above its cap, jewelry uses § 522(d)(4), listed household goods or musical instruments use § 522(d)(3), and trade tools may use § 522(d)(6); § 522(d)(5) remains an additional alternative in every instance.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not use 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3) for an unlisted category such as a firearm or jewelry, do not omit a specific paragraph because value exceeds its ceiling, and do not omit or repeat § 522(d)(5).

actual_parent_EC_guidance.when: OREGON is allowable and the asset is personal property.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.procedure: Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) as an independent general personal-property alternative even when a more specific Oregon exemption also applies, including for a vehicle or professionally prescribed health aid.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not substitute the general alternative for the specific category exemption, apply it to real property, or classify wearing apparel as household goods under § 18.345(1)(f).

actual_proposed_EC_guidance.when: OREGON is allowable and the asset is personal property.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.procedure: Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) as an independent general personal-property alternative even when a more specific Oregon exemption also applies, including for a vehicle, firearm, or professionally prescribed health aid. Retain the correct specific alternative: subsection (f) for household goods, subsection (d) for a vehicle, and § 18.362 for a qualifying firearm.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not substitute the general alternative for the specific category exemption, apply it to real property, classify wearing apparel as household goods under § 18.345(1)(f), or use vehicle subsection (d) for nonvehicles.

actual_parent_EC_guidance.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the property is held for personal rather than business use.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently as the any-other-property alternative, including when apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid also has a specific exemption. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, and (e) covers professionally prescribed health aids. A value above a limit does not eliminate either applicable alternative.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not use § 12-1001(d) for ordinary household property; it requires implements, professional books, or tools of the debtor's trade. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel under subsection (a), and do not omit subsection (b) merely because a specific subsection applies.

actual_proposed_EC_guidance.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the property is held for personal rather than business use.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently as the any-other-property alternative, including when apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid also has a specific exemption. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, and (e) covers professionally prescribed health aids. A value above a limit does not eliminate either applicable alternative. An object's name or ability to function as a tool does not establish trade use; subsection (d) requires facts showing use in the debtor's trade.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not use § 12-1001(d) for an ordinary personal-use tool or household property. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel under subsection (a), and do not omit subsection (b) merely because a specific subsection applies.

actual_parent_EC_guidance.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the property is held for personal rather than business use.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently as the any-other-property alternative, including when apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid also has a specific exemption. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, and (e) covers professionally prescribed health aids. A value above a limit does not eliminate either applicable alternative.
actual_parent_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not use § 12-1001(d) for ordinary household property; it requires implements, professional books, or tools of the debtor's trade. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel under subsection (a), and do not omit subsection (b) merely because a specific subsection applies.

actual_proposed_EC_guidance.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the debtor owns personal property, including property expressly identified as a tool of the debtor's trade.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently for every item of personal property, including when subsection (a), (c), (d), or (e) also applies. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, (d) covers an implement, professional book, or tool expressly used in the debtor's trade, and (e) covers a professionally prescribed health aid. A value above a limit does not eliminate an applicable alternative.
actual_proposed_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel, or a device that displays pictures as a family picture. Require express trade-use facts for subsection (d), and do not classify business machinery as a motor vehicle merely because it can move.
